desc: Heavily filtered, low-fidelity kick/snare chopped straight from a vinyl-sourced loop, all top-end rolled off.
reaper:
Vinyl VST on the drum bus -> ReaEQ (steep LPF 7-8kHz) -> CHOWTapeModel (warm saturation, slight wobble).

Vinyl (Year 1960, 33 RPM, Dust and Mechanical Noise up on the drum bus). Pultec HLF-3C (low-pass at 8kHz). Studer A800 (7.5 ips — the slow speed is what softens the top).
notes: Chop from a single sample source, not separate one-shots — the loop's own bleed and imperfect timing IS the sound.

desc: A dissonant, slightly detuned piano/strings sample loop — the defining RZA texture.
reaper:
Kontakt 8 (piano) pitched -15 to -30 cents -> ReaEQ (cut low-mids) -> Tape Cassette 2 (wobble).

Manley Massive Passive (low-mid band set to Cut, bell, gain well down — thins it right out). Oxide Tape (15 ips — the slow speed does the smearing).
notes: Detune by ear until it sits 'wrong' but musical. Leave sample noise/hiss in — don't clean it up.

desc: Layered, shouted ad-libs and posse chants sitting behind the lead verse.
reaper:
1176AE VST (attack 7, release 7 — both fully fast) -> Capitol Chambers VST (short slap) -> automate volume down under the lead verse.

1176 Rev A (20:1, attack 7, Input driven hard for real squash). Capitol Chambers (short slap room).
notes: Record 3-4 different voices/takes shouting the same ad-lib and stack them wide.

desc: A deep, mono, distorted 808/kick foundation under the chopped drums.
reaper:
bx_boom VST -> ParametricOD (light drive) -> mono-sum with kHs Channel Mixer.

bx_boom (sub generator, tuned to root note). bx_blackdist2 (light saturation for grit).
notes: Keep it mono and centered — it should be felt more than heard next to the chopped drum loop.

desc: The deep, sustained, almost-melodic 808 kick that IS the bassline in Miami bass.
reaper:
bx_boom VST (decay maxed) -> TDR Kotelnikov (light bus glue).

bx_boom (long decay, tuned to root). Manley Variable Mu (gentle glue).
notes: Tune the 808 to the actual bassline notes — it functions as the bass instrument, not just a drum.

desc: Rapid-fire 808 clap rolls and hi-hat rolls driving the energy into the drop.
reaper:
SSL G-Bus Compressor VST (4:1, attack 0.1ms, release 0.1s) -> ReaEQ (+3dB 10kHz shelf).

SSL G-Bus Compressor (4:1, fastest attack and release for pump on the rolls). Pultec EQP-1A (High Boost at 10kHz, boost dial to about 4).
notes: Program rolls with increasing velocity into the drop for that classic 'revving' effect.

desc: Shouted, group call-and-response hooks meant for a PA system and a crowd.
reaper:
API 2500 VST (4:1, attack 0.1ms, release 0.1s) -> ReaEQ (boost 2-4kHz for shout presence).

610-A Tube Preamp (drive hot). API 2500 (4:1, fast attack, Thrust on Loud — aggressive glue on the group vocal bus).
notes: Track it loud and slightly distorted at the source — the grit is the point, don't clean it up in the mix.

desc: Bright, punchy synth stabs and arpeggios in the Latin freestyle/electro tradition.
reaper:
Vital (saw/square unison) -> Kilohearts kHs Delay (1/8 slap) -> Kilohearts kHs Chorus.

Minimoog (bright saw). Waterfall Rotary Speaker (subtle movement). Ampex ATR-102 (15 ips for tape compression on the stabs — the slap comes from kHs Delay, not the tape).
notes: Short, staccato stabs on the off-beats. Bright and slightly harsh is correct for this era.

desc: The classic 808 cowbell, clap, and open hat pattern that defines early electro-rap.
reaper:
ReaComp (light glue) -> ReaEQ (gentle LPF ~12kHz).

dbx 160 (light glue on drum bus — Threshold down until it just moves, Compression low). Pultec HLF-3C (low-pass at 10kHz).
notes: Program it straight and mechanical — this era is about the machine feel, not human swing.

desc: A vocoded, robotic lead vocal line in the Egyptian Lover / Mantronix tradition.
reaper:
Graillon 3 VST3 (pitch-tracked robot mode) -> ReaEQ (boost 2-3kHz for intelligibility).

Auburn Sounds Graillon 3 (vocoder/robot mode). Manley Preamp (warmth going in).
notes: Feed it a simple, monophonic melodic phrase — complex chords get muddy through a vocoder.

desc: A simple, rolling, monophonic 808 or synth-bass pattern under the beat.
reaper:
bx_boom VST -> ReaEQ (HPF at 30Hz to keep it clean).

bx_boom (short-medium decay). SPL Free Ranger (subtle low-end EQ shaping).
notes: Keep the pattern simple and repetitive — 2-4 notes looped is authentic to the era.

desc: Multiple layered 808 claps for a wide, snappy backbeat.
reaper:
ReaEQ (presence boost) -> Kilohearts kHs Stereo (slight width increase).

Pultec MEQ-5 (High Peak at 5kHz, boost dial to about 5). Studio D Chorus (subtle width).
notes: Layer 2-3 clap samples at slightly different pitches/timings for width without a chorus effect.

desc: A dark, pitched-down, VHS-tape-quality drum loop sampled from horror soundtracks or old funk breaks.
reaper:
Pitch sample down 3-5 semitones -> CHOWTapeModel (heavy wobble) -> ReaEQ (LPF 6kHz).

Oxide Tape (15 ips — the slow speed does the smearing). Pultec HLF-3C (low-pass at 5kHz).
notes: Slow the whole loop 5-10 BPM below the sample's natural tempo for that dragging, sinister feel.

desc: An eerie, minor-key piano or choir stab, often reversed at the tail for a rising swell.
reaper:
Kontakt 8 (choir/piano) -> ReaEQ (mid scoop) -> Hitsville Chambers VST (dark).

Manley Massive Passive (mid band set to Cut, bell, bandwidth wide — hollows it out). Hitsville Chambers (dark, short reverb).
notes: Reverse a copy of the stab and crossfade it into the front of the hit for a rising swell before impact.

desc: The Three 6 signature — the same vocal line pitched up for hooks and pitched down for ad-libs.
reaper:
Graillon 3 VST3 x2 (one pitched up ~5st, one down ~5st with formant lowered) -> 1176 on the down-pitched layer.

Auburn Sounds Graillon 3 (formant + pitch, two instances at opposite settings). Fairchild 660 on the low layer.
notes: Keep the down-pitched 'demon' layer drier and more compressed than the up-pitched hook layer.

desc: A long, sustained, distorted sub bass drone running under the whole beat.
reaper:
bx_boom VST -> ParametricOD (subtle drive) -> ReaEQ (LPF at 100Hz).

bx_boom (max decay/sustain). bx_yellowdrive (light tube grit).
notes: Let it ring through chord changes rather than retriggering — the constant low drone builds dread.

desc: A rubbery, bouncing synth bass line that drives the whole Bay Area sound.
reaper:
Surge XT (bass patch, slight portamento) -> LA-3A VST (Compress mode, Peak Reduction up for 4-5dB of gain reduction) -> ReaEQ (boost 80-120Hz).

Minimoog (square/saw blend). Waterfall Rotary Speaker (subtle movement). LA-3A (glue).
notes: Add a short slide/glide between notes for the signature 'rubber band' bounce.

desc: Fast, syncopated hi-hat and rim patterns pushing the tempo forward.
reaper:
ReaComp (fast, light) -> ReaEQ (+2dB shelf at 10kHz).

SSL E-Channel Strip (light compression, Fast Attack out). Pultec EQP-1A (High Boost at 16kHz, boost dial to about 4).
notes: Program hats with alternating open/closed accents rather than a straight 16th pattern.

desc: Shouted, slang-heavy hooks meant to be chanted back at a show.
reaper:
CHANNEV VST (1073 + 1176 combined) -> ReaEQ (presence boost 3kHz).

Neve 1073 (drive the preamp gain hot). 1176 Rev A (20:1, attack 7 — fast catch on shouted peaks).
notes: Track multiple vocalists shouting the hook together in one pass for authentic crew energy.

desc: A bright, simple synth whistle or flute melody carrying the hook.
reaper:
Vital (triangle/sine) -> Kilohearts kHs Delay (dotted 8th) -> Ocean Way Studios Deluxe VST.

Pure sine/triangle wave. Ampex ATR-102 (30 ips for a clean tape print — the dotted-8th delay is kHs Delay's job). Ocean Way Studios Deluxe (studio room, mics pulled back for depth).
notes: Keep it a simple, singable, repetitive 4-8 note melody — it's the most important hook element in the mix.

desc: A warm, walking upright bass sample loop, often slightly swung.
reaper:
ReaEQ (boost 100-200Hz warmth) -> ReaComp (gentle 2:1) -> Capitol Chambers VST (short).

610-A Tube Preamp (warmth). Fairchild 670 (gentle glue). Capitol Chambers (subtle room).
notes: Chop the loop at the bar rather than the beat to preserve the natural swing/bounce of the original playing.

desc: Warm electric piano or jazz guitar chord stabs, sampled and looped.
reaper:
Kontakt 8 (Rhodes) -> ReaEQ (warmth boost) -> Lexicon 224 VST (plate).

Neve 1073 (low shelf at 220Hz, mid bell at 3.2kHz — those are the nearest real steps). Studio D Chorus (subtle width). Lexicon 224 (reverb).
notes: Keep chords sustained and let them breathe — this style relies on space between hits, not density.

desc: A relaxed, human-feeling drum loop with natural swing, not quantized-tight.
reaper:
ReaComp (2:1, slow attack) -> ReaEQ (gentle LPF).

SSL E-Channel Strip (light glue, Fast Attack out). Pultec HLF-3C (low-pass at 12kHz).
notes: If programming rather than sampling, manually nudge snare hits +/-10-15ms off grid for human feel.

desc: Laid-back, mid-volume, conversational vocal delivery typical of jazz-rap.
reaper:
1073 VST -> LA-2A VST (Compress mode, Peak Reduction for 3-4dB of gain reduction) -> Lexicon 224 VST (short plate, low mix).

Manley Preamp (warm gain). LA-2A (Compress mode, gentle Peak Reduction — its timing is fixed, there's nothing to set). Short plate reverb.
notes: Keep the vocal sitting IN the track, not on top of it — this genre favors blend over dominance.
